title: Symphony work in Cairo and Alexandria
summary: After Shanghai he played Shepheard's Hotel in Cairo and Alexandria, doubled in a symphony group and learned Boehm clarinet basics from Bonomi.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: in the reed section, you know. I'll switch off for a minute. Would you like to talk about your experiences with symphony orchestras over here?

Well, I was in, after I left Shanghai, as I told you, I went to Cairo, Alexandria. I mean, Cairo, Egypt, for six months, playing at the Shepherd's Hotel. And you had, we had a band of all the nations, we called them, because we had Greek. Papas, he played third alto in a band, and he also played classical music, also flute, double on flute, classical group. And the five hotels on Sundays, from eleven to one, they would play for tea like, you know. Tea dance. Yeah. And we'd form a symphony. All the guys doubled, you know, these musicians in Europe at the time, they were all great musicians. And so after being there six months, when I went to Alexandria, Egypt, at the Casinos in Bacchus, my instrument got out of whack, my Albert system clarinet. I had to send it to Paris to have it fixed. And Italian, Mr. Bonomi, who was playing clarinet in the symphony, he had two clarinets, and he loaned me his bohem. In fact, he taught me the rudiments of the instrument, and he gave me a lot of points in classical training. Had you been on Albert's system before, up to this point? Up to that point, yes. And then a couple of months, when my horn came back from France, well, I had forgotten all about the training. I'd forgotten it, but it seemed strange to me. In fact, I loved the other system much better, and it did me a lot of good. Then on Sundays, on, as I said, rehearsing with the band, they had me on third clarinet, playing third part sometime, but in the second. And by the end of the year, I was coming on pretty good with this type of music. And it was a wonderful experience for me, from when I came back to the States, playing different arrangements. You found it improved your reading and everything? Oh, it improved everything, sure. Playing and everything, reading and everything. That's right. Disappearance of reading. Yes, it was a good thing. Very good. Good training.
